theory.intro: A triangle is exactly half of a parallelogram (or rectangle) with the same base and height, so its area is half of base times height.
facts: The height is the **perpendicular** distance from the base to the opposite vertex, not a slanted side.
Area is measured in square units: cm$^{2}$, m$^{2}$.
steps: Identify the base and the perpendicular height (the dashed line at a right angle).
Multiply base $\times$ height, then halve the result.
Write the answer with squared units.

foundation.solution_text:
In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides meet at $90^{\circ}$, so they are the base and the height.
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$=\frac{9\times6}{2}$
$=27\text{ cm}^{2}$

The perpendicular height is still $5\text{ cm}$, even though it meets the base line outside the triangle.
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$=\frac{14\times5}{2}$
$=35\text{ cm}^{2}$

foundation.question_text: A rectangular block of land measuring $30\text{ m}$ long by $18\text{ m}$ wide is cut in half along a diagonal. Find the area of each triangular block in $\text{m}^{2}$.
foundation.solution_text:
Each triangle has the same base and height as the rectangle.
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$=\frac{30\times18}{2}$
$=270\text{ m}^{2}$

$A_{\text{left}}=\frac{12\times20}{2}$
$=120\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_{\text{right}}=\frac{18\times20}{2}$
$=180\text{ m}^{2}$
$180-120=60$
The difference is $60\text{ m}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: Triangle $A$ has a base of $12\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $7\text{ cm}$. Triangle $B$ has a base of $14\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area, and by how many $\text{cm}^{2}$?
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{A}=\frac{12\times7}{2}$
$=42\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{B}=\frac{14\times6}{2}$
$=42\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both triangles have an area of $42\text{ cm}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: A triangular lawn has a base of $9\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ m}$. Turf is sold only in rolls that each cover $5\text{ m}^{2}$. How many rolls must be bought?
mastery.solution_text:
$A=\frac{bh}{2}$
$=\frac{9\times6}{2}$
$=27\text{ m}^{2}$
$27\div5=5.4$
Rolls cannot be split, so $6$ rolls must be bought.
